newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends higher as upswing continues.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends higher as upswing continues.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures rose sharply on Tuesday, resuming its recent upswing after a two-day pause, as supply concerns persisted, traders said.

March delivery jumped 2.90 cents per lb on the day, to 139.50 cents, after ranging between 140.20 and 136.50 cents. Second-position May finished 2.85 cents higher, at 134.60 cents, while the outer months closed up 2.85 to 4.20 cents.
Market sources said today's run up was helped along by a report from German trader Bernhard Rothfos GmbH, which forecast a global production deficit of 1.5 million bags in 1996/97.
After analysing consumption and exports according to coffee types, Rothfos forecast a three million bag deficit in arabicas in the 96/97 season.
"It (the Rothfos report) just added one more piece of bullish news to the pie," one trader said.

Dealers said speculative and trade buying accounted for much of the day's gains, but light origin selling capped the upside and prevented the March contract from piercing key resistance at 142.60 cents, its life-of-contract high.
While some traders said the market's firm finish indicated it was poised to set new highs, other sources said the market is still overbought.
"It should have corrected more than it has," Smith Barney analyst Walter Spilka said. "It is tighter than it was, but there is still a lot of coffee to come into the market."
Spilka said the resolution of the dockworkers strike in Colombia would eventually bring exportable coffee held over by the work stoppage into the marketplace.
An auction of 200,000 60-kg bags of Brazilian government coffee stocks Feb. 5 should also weigh on the market, he added.
Volume Tuesday reached an estimated 7,543 lots.
